summary: Host OpenTelemetry pipeline: local span summaries plus opt-in OTLP trace export configured by environment variables and Settings.
context_hints: Only this directory depends on the OpenTelemetry SDK; instrumented code (e.g. runtime/host/lib/session-tracing.ts) uses @opentelemetry/api only.
Every finished span is written locally as a span.end LogRecord; OTLP export stays off unless CLASH_ENABLE_TELEMETRY is on.
Keys follow Claude Code's model: the master switch plus standard OTEL_* names; a key present in Settings wins over the environment, and an empty Settings value cancels it.
Settings values are resolved in memory and never written to process.env, so agent processes started by the Host do not inherit them.
Spans carry ids, counts and durations only; never prompts, tool arguments or tool output.
The Settings contract (keys, view, PATCH body) is the Zod schema in packages/shared-types/src/telemetry.ts.

Local clients (the GUI renderer) export with the official OTLP/HTTP JSON exporter to POST /api/v1/local/otlp/v1/traces; the Host decodes spans back into ReadableSpan and feeds its own processors, so client spans share the local summary and the configured exporter, and credentials never reach the client.

key_files.resolve.ts: Pure resolution of environment + Settings into an export decision, with per-key value sources. OTel specification defaults live here.
key_files.exporters.ts: Official OTLP exporters keyed by protocol; hides OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* endpoint/header env during construction so Settings stay authoritative.
key_files.processors.ts: SpanLogProcessor (span.end LogRecords) and SwitchableSpanProcessor (hot-swappable export slot).
key_files.pipeline.ts: NodeTracerProvider assembly, serialized export swaps, ingest() for client spans, and the process-wide installHostTelemetry singleton.
key_files.config-store.ts: Telemetry Settings as a LocalConfigResource: config.yaml for plain keys, credentials.json for headers, pipeline reapplied after each update.
key_files.otlp-ingest.ts: Decoder for OTLP JSON ExportTraceServiceRequest into SDK ReadableSpans, with per-request limits from the SDK environment defaults; tested by round-tripping the official JsonTraceSerializer.
